content: Faidherbia albida, also known as Apple-ring Acacia, Ana Tree, or Winter Thorn, is a species of tree native to Africa and the Middle East. It was previously classified under the genus Acacia and has since been introduced to regions such as India and Pakistan. This tree is characterized by its thorny structure, growing to heights of 6 to 30 meters, with a trunk diameter of up to 2 meters. Its deep-penetrating taproot system makes it highly resistant to drought conditions. The bark of the tree is gray and becomes fissured with age. Each kilogram of its seeds contains approximately 11,000 seeds. Faidherbia albida is not considered a threatened species and thrives in areas receiving 250 to 600 millimeters of rainfall annually. In the Bambara language, the tree is referred to as balanzan and holds cultural significance as the official tree of Ségou, a city located along the Niger River in central Mali. According to local legend, Ségou is home to 4,444 balanzan trees, with an additional missing tree whose location remains unknown. Cultivation and Uses Faidherbia albida plays a significant role in beekeeping, as its flowers provide essential forage for bees at the end of the rainy season, a time when most other plants in the Sahel region are not in bloom. The seed pods of the tree are highly valued as livestock feed and are particularly used as camel fodder in Nigeria. The wood of the tree is utilized for making canoes, pestles, and firewood, with a density of approximately 560 kg/m³ at a water content of 12%. Additionally, the tree is employed in nitrogen fixation, erosion control for crops, and as a source of food, drink, and medicine. Unlike most other trees, Faidherbia albida sheds its leaves during the rainy season. This unique characteristic makes it highly beneficial in agroforestry, as it can grow among field crops without shading them. The leaves of the tree contain the psychoactive compound dimethyltryptamine (DMT). Medicinal Uses Faidherbia albida possesses medicinal properties and is used in the treatment of various infections, including respiratory infections, malaria, and fevers. It is also effective in addressing digestive system disorders. The bark of the tree is used in dental hygiene, and its extract is applied to alleviate toothache. Furthermore, the extract is utilized in treating ocular infections in farm animals.
